title: NBA sports product and research landscape sources
scope: Independent bounded research for 12-hour NBA augmented-video agent; no development, no external contact
source_policy: Primary publisher/product documents, official technical documentation, original research and dataset maintainer material; marketing is not treated as independent efficacy evidence

sources.title: NBA Powered by AWS
supports: Lists Shot Difficulty, Defensive Pressure, Gravity and Leverage in the NBA advanced statistics programme.
sources.limitations: Product description; not independent accuracy evaluation.

sources.title: NBA selects AWS as official cloud and cloud AI partner for basketball innovation
supports: Shot Difficulty considers shooter setup, position and defensive contest.
Gravity concerns attention drawn from defenders and opportunities for teammates.
Play Finder is described as an individual-play search capability; some fan-facing versions are explicitly future iterations.
sources.limitations: Do not treat every announced feature as publicly available or proven at arbitrary-video recognition.

sources.title: Intro to Expected Field Goal Percentage
supports: Player-agnostic xFG definition.
sources.limitations: Definition differs from a shorthand in the AWS Leverage article; use competition data dictionary.

sources.title: Intro to Gravity
supports: Gravity compares actual with expected defensive attention.
sources.limitations: Cannot infer an official Gravity score from nearest-defender distance alone.

sources.title: Intro to Defensive Pressure Score
supports: Higher pressure does not necessarily mean better defense.
sources.limitations: Specific scoring implementation must follow the supplied metric version.

sources.title: How the NBA and AWS built an AI system to measure what actually wins basketball games
supports: Leverage uses actual versus counterfactual outcomes, with credit across players.
It combines win probability and contextual attribution, including Shot Difficulty.
The article reports LightGBM trained on about 3,700 games and 500,000 possessions; this is not a hackathon-reproducible model specification.
Reported Shot Difficulty latency is 10–12 seconds; subsecond latency is an optimization target.
sources.limitations: System-provider claims, not independent benchmark. Describes shooter skill in xFG shorthand; NBA specialist definition is player-agnostic.

sources.title: NBA and Genius Sports / Second Spectrum Expand Partnership
supports: 2023 partnership expansion covers League Pass augmentation and team analytics.
Graphics are based on optical on-court data.
Dragon is described in this release as research and development, not completed universal deployment.
sources.limitations: Do not cite 2023 roadmap wording as proof of present-day feature coverage.

sources.title: GeniusIQ offering fans a new game-watching experience at FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup
supports: 2025 Lausanne case uses 12 strategically placed iPhones for optical tracking.
Broadcast overlays include player speed, shot charts and momentum.
sources.limitations: Vendor-reported deployment; no independent accuracy measurements; multiple fixed cameras are not one television video.

sources.title: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor
supports: Double-clicking a plotted shot opens its associated video clip.
sources.limitations: Documents workflow, not automatic tactical interpretation.

sources.title: Basketball game analysis | Hudl Assist
supports: Reports link data points to video and offer game/season filtering.
Shot charts expose floor-area percentages.
sources.limitations: Marketing product page; no numerical accuracy evidence retrieved.

sources.title: Synergy Basketball FAQs
supports: Synergy possession context is manually tagged.
Synergy enriched analytics include play types, pick-and-roll details, lineups and shot coordinates.
Synergy is post-game, distinct from official live event data; FAQ says it should not be considered an official data source.
sources.limitations: Coverage, package, season access and ID mapping differ from other Sportradar APIs.

sources.title: Automated Video Solutions
supports: Describes automatic capture, production and streaming with graphical overlays.
Lists automated camera installations across 36 arenas in French basketball’s top two tiers.
sources.limitations: Broadcast quality is promotional wording; full hardware workflow is not reproduced by an editing prototype.

sources.title: HomeCourt
supports: Basketball training app offers shot tracking and skill feedback using mobile-device cameras.
sources.limitations: Training use case is not equivalent to full NBA broadcast understanding.

sources.title: Setup FAQ
supports: Improved operating conditions include good light, hoop net, clear court lines and a single shooter.
sources.limitations: Strong evidence that capture conditions matter; not an accuracy benchmark.

sources.title: NBA and Sony’s Hawk-Eye Innovations launch strategic partnership powering next generation tracking technology
supports: Partnership begins with 2023–24 deployment of 3D optical tracking.
The release distinguishes tracking and pose applications from future automated officiating opportunities.
sources.limitations: Not evidence that a single broadcast camera yields equivalent 3D data or that every future officiating use shipped.

sources.title: WNBA Inside the Game, powered by AWS: AI Meets the Next Era of Women’s Basketball
supports: Explains Gravity as actual pressure minus expected pressure conditioned on offensive spacing and ball position.
Includes normalized Gravity descriptions and an applied enhanced-broadcast use case.
sources.limitations: WNBA article is a related implementation, not the NBA challenge schema. Its heading and body give different frame-rate wording; no frame-rate claim is carried into the recommendation.

sources.title: POINTWISE: Predicting Points and Valuing Decisions in Real Time with NBA Optical Tracking Data
supports: Proposes expected possession value from player tracking and models pre-terminal decisions.
Reports application to 2012–13 season tracking data.
sources.limitations: Research model; not publicly downloadable current official NBA service or a shortcut using only box scores.

sources.title: A Multiresolution Stochastic Process Model for Predicting Basketball Possession Outcomes
supports: Uses optical player tracking and models continuous movements plus discrete possession events to estimate expected points.
sources.limitations: No claim of direct equivalence with modern xFG, Gravity or Leverage.

sources.title: Characterizing the spatial structure of defensive skill in professional basketball
supports: Uses player tracking and spatial/statistical modelling for defensive analysis.
sources.limitations: Defensive contribution is model-dependent; nearest-defender proximity alone is insufficient proof of responsibility.

sources.title: pbpstats Documentation
supports: Adds lineups and possession start/end context to play-by-play.
Corrects event order in some common cases.
sources.limitations: Derived parsing can need manual overrides; docs are not evidence every historical game parses perfectly.

sources.title: nba_data repository
supports: Provides downloadable seasonal PBP and shot-detail archives collected from NBA/PBPStats endpoints.
Repository advertises Apache 2.0.
sources.limitations: Community provenance; upstream rights do not follow automatically from repository license. README season range can lag file list.

sources.title: nba_data archive index
supports: Contains direct tar.xz archive URLs for data variants and seasons.
sources.limitations: This is the index; file download checks are separately recorded below.

sources.title: nba_data field dictionary
supports: Describes shot coordinates, event IDs, period/clock, make flag and PBPStats possession fields.
sources.limitations: Some fields are undocumented. Verify coordinate units and ID joins before use.

sources.title: nba_data LICENSE
supports: Repository contains the Apache License 2.0 text.
sources.limitations: Does not itself demonstrate that the uploader can sublicense all underlying NBA data or video.

sources.title: nba_api repository
supports: Community Python NBA API client is MIT-licensed.
sources.limitations: Library software license does not grant NBA data usage rights or availability guarantees.

sources.title: nba_api live PlayByPlay endpoint documentation
supports: Documents CDN endpoint format, game-ID parameter and event fields.
Fields are conditional by action type.
sources.limitations: Documented endpoint returned HTTP 403 in our target-game test.

sources.title: NBA Game Play-by-Play
supports: Documents event locations on a 1128 by 600 inch court, scores, clocks and event descriptions.
On-court participants are conditional on the track_on_court flag.
API access uses trial or production access levels.
sources.limitations: Not raw player-and-ball trajectories; not proof our account has access.

sources.title: Your Account
supports: Default trials are 30 days, 1,000 rolling-period requests and 1 QPS.
Production access is for customers and some products are not self-issued trials.
sources.limitations: Quotas may differ by package; no account was created and no purchase made.

sources.title: Sportradar US Master Terms and Conditions
supports: Free trials are for internal evaluation and do not authorize publication/display of data.
Paid use is tied to products and properties in the order form.
sources.limitations: Terms dated August 5, 2026. Competition-specific permissions must be obtained from organizer documentation.

sources.title: NBA-Player-Movements
supports: Repository contains visualization code and a 2016 raw SportVU logs directory.
sources.limitations: No clear data redistribution license was verified in this review; not selected for default deliverable.

sources.title: Terms of Use: NBA Statistics
supports: Statistics have specific usage restrictions.
sources.limitations: Consult Section 9 and competition-specific authorization; no legal conclusion about a particular competition grant is made.

unverified: Official challenge video and deep metric files have not been received.
Exact competition scoring weights and data/video publication scope are not known.
No HomeCourt, Synergy, Hudl, Genius or Hawk-Eye accuracy benchmark was independently reproduced.
No unofficial source is assumed to contain modern official xFG, Gravity and Leverage.
recommended_data_policy: Prefer organizer-authorized files; use conspicuously labelled synthetic calibration assets before delivery; keep raw restricted data out of public code repository unless explicitly permitted.
